description: FMT* (Fast Marching Tree) draws one batch of random samples and then grows a tree outward from the start in order of cost-to-come, like a wavefront. Each step takes the cheapest open node `z`. Each unvisited neighbour `x` of `z` connects to the open neighbour that gives `x` the lowest cost, and only that one motion is checked for collisions; if the check fails, `x` waits for a later step instead of trying the next-best parent. This *lazy* rule needs far fewer collision checks than RRT* or PRM*. FMT* is still *asymptotically optimal*: as the batch grows, its cost converges in probability to the optimum.

papers.authors: Lucas Janson, Edward Schmerling, Ashley Clark, Marco Pavone
papers.title: Fast Marching Tree: A Fast Marching Sampling-Based Method for Optimal Motion Planning in Many Dimensions
papers.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research
